beliefs: f removes all whitespace characters (space, tab, newline, and Unicode whitespace) from the string [E1, E2, E3, E7, E9]
f lowercases all letters using Unicode-aware lowercasing [E1, E2, E3, E10]
f capitalizes the first character of the result only if the original string's first character is not whitespace [E2, E3, E8]
leading whitespace (space, tab, etc.) prevents capitalization of the first remaining character [E2, E3, E8]
empty string and all-whitespace strings map to empty string [E1, E2, E3]
digits and punctuation are left unchanged [E1, E2, E3]
the capitalize-first rule uses titlecase-uppercasing of the first char (e.g. ǆ becomes ǅ), not full uppercase [E11, E13]
capitalization is applied to the first surviving character via titlecase-uppercase only (not full str.capitalize), since ẞ (U+1E9E) stays as-is rather than becoming 'Ss' [E12, E13]
the rest of the string is lowercased before capitalization, so mixed-case non-ASCII like Ǆ becomes ǆ then ǅ [E12]
titlecase-uppercasing the first char uses str.title() semantics, which for ß yields 'Ss' and for ligatures like ﬀ/ﬁ yields 'Ff'/'Fi' [E11, E13]
notes: E13 shows ẞ (U+1E9E) stays as-is rather than becoming 'Ss', so the first-char transform is titlecase (str.title on the char), not str.capitalize. Changed the ß special-case to a general first.title() call, which already handles ß→Ss, ﬀ→Ff, ﬁ→Fi, ǆ→ǅ, and leaves ẞ unchanged.
